whatItIs.text: A thick slice from beside the pig's rib — loin chop, rib chop, or shoulder chop — fried, grilled, or braised across half the world's kitchens.

historyNote.text: The English term dates to about 1752 and the French côtelette de porc to the 14th century, but chops only became widely popular in the 19th century; Mrs Beeton gave two recipes in 1861, and old cookbooks insisted on cooking pork to death — modern breeding has made the safe, juicy chop possible.

howToChoose.text: Choose chops with pink, marbled flesh and a thin fat edge; bone-in chops stay juicier, and shoulder chops are the budget-friendly flavour winner for braising.

storage.text: Raw pork keeps on the coldest shelf; marinate in the fridge, never on the counter.

useItUp.text: Leftover chop goes into salads or a pan sauce — apple, mustard, or cream.

substitutions.note: much leaner; cook faster or it dries
